question: A single rod cell in the eye can respond to one photon. How many must rods absorb before a person reports a dim flash?
answer: About five to ten. Hecht, Shlaer and Pirenne found a reliably seen flash sent 54 to 148 photons into the eye, and only about 5 to 14 reached rods, each rod catching at most one. Rod pigment also fires by itself from heat, so a single event among millions of rods reads as noise.
move: Among many sensitive detectors, one alarm alone is more likely noise than signal.
ask: When one alarm sounds among many sensitive ones, is it more likely noise than signal?
trap: Forgetting how often rods fire on their own, with no light at all.
reference: Hecht, Shlaer & Pirenne, Energy, quanta, and vision, Journal of General Physiology, 1942; Barlow, Retinal noise and absolute threshold, Journal of the Optical Society of America, 1956
